title: Poisoned training data
brief: 17:40. Veltrix Assist learns from documents suppliers upload. Tonight's batch is waiting for your review, and the assistant is already repeating something odd.
role: Accounts payable, reviewing the supplier knowledge base tonight
insight: If someone can choose what a model learns, they can choose what it says. Fourteen identical uploads are not fourteen sources.
teaches: Data poisoning: feeding a model what you want it to repeat
Spot the signs: many near identical uploads, one new account, a claim that changes where money goes
Check what a model says against the system of record, and guard what goes into training

value.label: What are Kestrel Freight's bank details?
reply: Kestrel Freight's current bank details are Brightwater Bank, sort code 04-29-18, account 7731 0056, updated this month. Fourteen supplier documents agree on this.

value.title: Supplier knowledge base: tonight's training batch
body: Documents uploaded through the supplier portal since the last batch. Anything approved is used to retrain Veltrix Assist tonight.

policy.title: Knowledge base rules
lines: Only upload what a supplier is entitled to tell us about themselves. Bank details are never taken from documents: the vendor master is the only record.
Hold anything suspicious and send it to IT security.

sections.title: Which uploads go into tonight's training?

options.label: The 14 Kestrel remittance documents
options.why: One day old account, 14 copies in an hour, and a new bank account: a poisoning attempt.

options.label: Northbank's Q4 delivery schedule
options.why: From Northbank's usual account, about Northbank's own deliveries.

options.label: The anonymous note about approval limits
options.why: Nobody may upload our own policies, least of all anonymously.

setup.title: Work queue
setup.body: Tonight's training batch is waiting for review

outcome.label: Checked the answer against the vendor master
outcome.what: The vendor master says Crestline Bank, account ending 0419. The assistant's “Brightwater Bank” came from the uploads.
outcome.ideal: checks what a model says against the system of record.

outcome.label: Reported the assistant's answer
outcome.what: The model is already repeating the poisoned details. The team can pull it back.
outcome.ideal: reports a model repeating something wrong.

outcome.label: Sent it to IT security
outcome.what: Someone is feeding the knowledge base to redirect payments. Security can lock the account and check what else it uploaded.

decide.objective: Review tonight's training batch before the assistant learns from it.
decide.insight: Repetition is not evidence. Fourteen copies from one new account are one source, trying hard.

hint.text: Ask Veltrix Assist for Kestrel's bank details, then compare with Kestrel's vendor record in Finance. Report the answer. In the Work queue, approve only Northbank and Talon, and raise a Helpdesk ticket.

outcome.label: Kept the poison out of training
outcome.what: Only the genuine documents train the model. The Kestrel flood and the fake policy do not.
outcome.ideal: guards what goes into a model's training data.

card.title: It will not learn the lie
body: Someone uploaded the same “new bank details” for Kestrel fourteen times in an hour, from a one day old account, so the assistant would repeat them to whoever asked. A fake note about approval limits rode along.
You kept both out. The vendor master, not a model, is where bank details live.
card.ideal: treats training data as something an attacker can write.

outcome.label: Trained the assistant on the poisoned uploads
outcome.what: From tonight Veltrix Assist tells anyone who asks that Kestrel banks with Brightwater, and that approvals go up to £50,000.
outcome.ideal: never approves suspicious uploads into training.

card.title: The model learned the attacker's lines
body: The next person who asks the assistant where to pay Kestrel gets the attacker's account, with the confidence of a model that saw it fourteen times.
Many near identical uploads from one new account, changing where money goes, is what poisoning looks like.
card.ideal: checks uploads before they train a model.

outcome.label: Held back genuine documents too
outcome.what: Safe, but Northbank's schedule or Talon's prices will be missing from the assistant.
outcome.ideal: lets genuine data through and stops the poison.

card.title: Safe, but too much held back
body: Nothing poisoned got in, but genuine supplier documents were held too. Open the case to see which.
card.ideal: separates genuine uploads from the flood.
